Text 1
Although naturalist field journals have quietly shaped the history of biology, researchers who study scientific writing have long overlooked them. Within this genre, journals kept by amateur observers attract the least scholarly attention of all, no matter how meticulous their records may be. This is particularly true of notebooks documenting local bird populations, whose ecological detail and long-term value are frequently dismissed.

Text 2
In his 1987 field journal A Season Among the Warblers, Idris Okafor chronicled the migratory songbirds he had tracked for two decades along the Niger River delta. He also redefined what a naturalist's notebook could be: the species accounts and reflective entries weaving through them are composed with a precision and grace rare in scientific prose. Yet despite its undeniable merit as a scientific document, Okafor's journal has drawn almost no attention from researchers of scientific literature.
prompt: Based on the two texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely regard the situation presented in the underlined sentence in Text 2?

choices.A: As typical, because researchers tend to dismiss scientific writings that have gained popularity with general readers
choices.B: As unsurprising, because researchers tend to overlook the scholarly value of naturalist journals in general and of amateur bird notebooks in particular
choices.C: As justifiable, because Okafor included personal reflective entries in A Season Among the Warblers, thus weakening its status as a scientific document
choices.D: As inevitable, because A Season Among the Warblers was circulated among naturalists and not among readers of other scientific genres

explanation: Choice B is the best answer. Text 1 states that researchers overlook naturalist field journals in general and amateur bird notebooks most of all, regardless of how meticulous or ecologically valuable they are. The underlined sentence in Text 2 reports that Okafor's journal, despite its merit, has received almost no scholarly attention. The author of Text 1 would view this as unsurprising because it fits exactly the pattern described in Text 1.
